key_insight: Biomechanically grounded 3D joint-angle estimates from single-camera infant videos enabled AI prediction of selective motor control scores and separation of infants with versus without cerebral palsy.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support scalable infant movement assessment, but its cerebral palsy discrimination remained below expert clinician scoring.
method: BB3D estimates infant 3D joint-angle trajectories from single-camera video.
A spatio-temporal transformer was pretrained on 1,000+ recordings and fine-tuned on 550 videos from 350 infants.
The model predicts individual BabyOSCAR items and total scores without training on diagnosis.
evidence_signal: Evaluation showed 17.5 mm median aligned joint-center error in 17 infants; on held-out recordings, BabyOSCAR total correlation was 0.86, while cerebral palsy discrimination AUC was 0.86 versus 0.67 for a 2D baseline and 0.97 for expert scores.
watch_item: Within-site evaluation and a small 3D validation cohort leave cross-site generalizability and clinical implementation uncertain.
paper_title: Biomechanically Grounded Prediction of Selective Motor Control and Clinical Outcomes from Infant Video
